title: ESP32-Based Energy Monitor
problem: Household and small-installation energy use is usually only visible on a monthly bill, which is far too late to act on. The goal is a clamp-on monitor that reads real power, logs it continuously, and survives the network dropping.
approach: Split-core current transformer into a burden resistor, sampled by the ESP32 ADC with a proper anti-alias front end and a calibrated phase correction. RMS and real power are computed on-device rather than streaming raw samples, then published over MQTT with local buffering for outages.
results_note: Not yet measured. Accuracy figures will be published as a bench test against a calibrated reference meter, with the conditions stated.
